name: Stellantis
desc: Multinational carmaker producing Jeep, Ram, Peugeot, Fiat, Citroën, Opel, Alfa Romeo and Maserati vehicles for consumers and fleets.
markets: Sells cars and light commercial vehicles across Europe, North America, South America, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Portfolio of mass and premium brands across Europe and the Americas; F1 offers global brand reach and B2B hospitality.
changed: Formed in 2021 by merger of PSA Group and Fiat Chrysler Automobiles

name: Leapmotor
desc: Chinese maker of battery-electric and range-extender passenger cars sold in China and, via Stellantis, internationally.
markets: China core market; exports through Leapmotor International, a Stellantis-led joint venture, to Europe and other regions.
rationale: Budget EV brand building awareness in Europe; F1 could support launch marketing alongside Stellantis distribution.
changed: Stellantis acquired about 20% stake in 2023 and formed Leapmotor International joint venture

name: NIO
desc: Chinese premium electric vehicle maker selling NIO, ONVO and firefly cars, with battery-swap stations and direct retail.
markets: Mainly China; also sells in several European markets including Germany, Norway, Netherlands, Sweden and Denmark.
rationale: Tech-focused premium EV brand seeking international awareness; F1 fits technology and premium positioning, though losses limit budgets.

name: BYD Company
desc: Chinese manufacturer of electric and plug-in hybrid cars, buses, trucks, batteries and electronic components.
industry: new energy vehicle and battery maker
markets: Sells vehicles across China, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Middle East; buses and batteries also in North America.
rationale: Fast international expansion and heavy sports sponsorship (UEFA Euro); F1 offers global consumer reach in its growth markets.

name: Cummins
desc: Designs and manufactures diesel, natural gas, electric and hydrogen engines, powertrains, generators and filtration for vehicle and industrial customers.
markets: Customers in about 190 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa.
rationale: Global B2B engineering brand with motorsport heritage; F1 offers technology showcase and hospitality for OEM customers.

name: Forvia
desc: Automotive supplier of seating, interiors, lighting, electronics and clean mobility systems for carmakers worldwide.
markets: Supplies carmakers across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and South America from plants in many countries.
rationale: Global supplier with Hella lighting brand; F1 could serve B2B hospitality and engineering credibility with carmaker customers.
changed: Renamed from Faurecia to Forvia after acquiring Hella in 2022

name: Nissan Motor
desc: Japanese carmaker selling Nissan and Infiniti passenger cars, SUVs, electric vehicles and light commercial vehicles.
markets: Sells worldwide, with major markets in Japan, North America, China, Europe and Middle East.
rationale: Global consumer brand with Formula E presence; restructuring after heavy losses limits near-term sponsorship budgets.
changed: Merger talks with Honda ended in 2025; restructuring under way

name: Valeo
desc: Automotive supplier of driver-assistance sensors, lighting, thermal systems, electrified powertrains and aftermarket parts for carmakers.
markets: Operates in about 29 countries serving carmakers across Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Americas, plus the aftermarket.
rationale: Technology supplier with endurance-racing links; F1 offers engineering showcase and hospitality for carmaker clients.

name: XPeng
desc: Chinese maker of smart electric cars with in-house driver-assistance software, also developing flying cars and humanoid robots.
markets: China main market; exports to Europe, Middle East and Asia-Pacific markets, with offices in California and Munich.
rationale: Tech-forward EV brand expanding in Europe; F1 offers technology storytelling and international awareness.

name: Polestar
desc: Swedish electric performance car brand selling the Polestar 2, 3, 4 and 5 online and through retail spaces.
markets: Sells in over 25 markets across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific; cars built in China, US and South Korea.
rationale: Design-led premium EV brand needing awareness; F1 fits, but continued losses and parent support constrain budgets.
changed: Listed via SPAC merger in 2022; Volvo Cars transferred most of its stake to Geely in 2024

name: TE Connectivity
desc: Designs and manufactures connectors, sensors and harnesses for automotive, industrial, aerospace, medical, energy and data-centre customers.
markets: Customers in about 140 countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Component supplier to every major carmaker; F1 offers engineering showcase and B2B hospitality.

name: Eaton Corporation
desc: Power management company making electrical equipment, data-centre power systems, hydraulics, aerospace and vehicle components.
markets: Sells to customers in more than 175 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Diversified B2B brand with data-centre and electrification push; F1 plausible for B2B hospitality but not obvious.

name: Aptiv
desc: Automotive technology supplier of vehicle architecture, connectors, wiring, active safety and software for carmakers.
markets: Presence in about 50 countries, serving carmakers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Software and electrical architecture supplier with motorsport history in Formula E; F1 offers technology showcase.
changed: Announced in 2025 a plan to spin off its Electrical Distribution Systems business

name: Adient
desc: Designs and manufactures complete automotive seats, seat structures, foam and trim for global carmakers.
markets: Plants in more than 30 countries supplying carmakers across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B seating supplier with little brand marketing; F1 possible only as hospitality for carmaker customers.
changed: Spun off from Johnson Controls in 2016

name: AUTO1 Group
desc: Online used-car platform buying cars from private sellers and dealers and selling to dealers and consumers via Autohero.
markets: Operates in about 30 European countries; no verified plans outside Europe.
rationale: European consumer brand Autohero growing; F1 could support pan-European awareness, though focus is cost-driven.

name: Avatr
desc: Chinese premium smart electric vehicle brand selling SUVs and saloons developed with Huawei and CATL technology.
markets: Mainly China; has begun exports to selected markets in Asia and Middle East.
rationale: Rising Chinese EV brand starting exports; F1 plausible for international awareness but early-stage abroad.

name: BRP
desc: Canadian maker of snowmobiles, personal watercraft, off-road vehicles and three-wheel motorcycles under Ski-Doo, Sea-Doo, Can-Am and Lynx.
markets: Sells through dealers in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Powersports brand with motorsport marketing culture; F1 offers global consumer reach to performance-minded buyers.
changed: Spun off from Bombardier in 2003

name: Geely Holding Group
desc: Chinese automotive group owning Geely Auto, Volvo Cars, Zeekr, Lynk & Co, Lotus, LEVC and Polestar stakes.
markets: Group brands sell across China, Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Global multi-brand group with premium marques and international ambitions; F1 offers worldwide brand reach.

name: Jaguar Land Rover
desc: British maker of luxury cars and SUVs under Range Rover, Defender, Discovery and Jaguar brands.
markets: Sells worldwide, with major markets in UK, North America, China, Europe and Middle East.
rationale: Luxury brands with Formula E experience; F1 fits premium positioning and electric Jaguar relaunch.
changed: Owned by Tata Motors since 2008

name: Magna International
desc: Canadian automotive supplier making body structures, seating, mirrors, powertrains and contract-assembled vehicles for carmakers.
markets: Operations across North America, Europe and Asia serving global carmakers.
rationale: Major supplier and contract vehicle builder; F1 offers engineering showcase and hospitality for carmaker clients.

name: Geely Automobile Holdings
desc: Listed carmaking arm of Geely Holding, producing Geely, Lynk & Co and Zeekr passenger vehicles.
markets: Mainly China; exports to Middle East, Asia, Latin America, Eastern Europe and Western Europe via Lynk & Co and Zeekr.
rationale: Growing exporter with premium Zeekr brand; F1 could support international brand building.
changed: Took Zeekr private and absorbed it as a wholly owned subsidiary in 2025

name: Goodyear Tire & Rubber
desc: US tyre maker selling Goodyear and Cooper tyres to consumers, fleets and carmakers, plus retail service centres.
markets: Sells across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Iconic tyre brand with deep motorsport heritage; F1 offers consumer reach, though Pirelli is the exclusive F1 tyre supplier.
changed: Sold Dunlop brand rights to Sumitomo Rubber and off-the-road tyre business to Yokohama in 2025

name: VinFast
desc: Vietnamese maker of electric cars, electric scooters and buses sold to consumers and fleets.
markets: Vietnam core market; sells in North America, Europe and Asia; plant opened in India in 2025.
rationale: Ambitious international EV brand needing awareness; F1 fits, though continued losses limit budgets.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq via SPAC merger in 2023

name: Autoliv
desc: World's largest maker of airbags, seatbelts and steering wheels, supplied to carmakers worldwide.
markets: Plants in about 25 countries supplying carmakers in Europe, Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Safety technology story suits F1, but B2B brand with limited marketing; plausible hospitality fit.

name: Volvo Cars
desc: Swedish premium carmaker producing Volvo SUVs, estates and saloons, including electric models, for consumers and fleets.
markets: Sells worldwide, with major markets in Europe, US, China and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Premium global brand with safety and electrification focus; F1 offers premium audience reach.

name: ZF Group
desc: German supplier of transmissions, chassis, driver assistance, electric drives and commercial vehicle systems to vehicle makers.
markets: Operates in around 30 countries serving car, truck and industrial customers worldwide.
rationale: Engineering brand with motorsport heritage; F1 offers technology showcase, though restructuring may limit budgets.

name: Constellium
desc: Produces rolled and extruded aluminium products for aerospace, automotive and packaging manufacturers.
markets: Plants in Europe and North America serving aerospace, automotive and can-sheet customers.
rationale: B2B metals supplier with lightweighting story; F1 link plausible but not obvious.

name: Subaru Corporation
desc: Japanese maker of Subaru all-wheel-drive cars and SUVs, plus aerospace products for defence and commercial aircraft.
markets: Mostly North America; also sells in Japan, Australia, Europe and other Asian markets.
rationale: Consumer brand with rally heritage, strongest in US; F1 plausible through US races but not obvious.
changed: Renamed from Fuji Heavy Industries in 2017

name: Zipline International
desc: Designs, builds and operates autonomous delivery drones for medical supplies, retail and food deliveries.
markets: Operates in the US, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire and Japan.
rationale: Technology brand scaling US consumer deliveries; F1 plausible as tech showcase but early for large sponsorship.

name: Bolt
desc: Mobility platform offering ride-hailing, scooter and bike rental, food and grocery delivery and car sharing.
markets: Over 50 countries in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America.
rationale: Consumer brand active in sports sponsorship across Europe and Africa; F1 offers broad urban audience reach.

name: Knorr-Bremse
desc: German maker of braking and safety systems for rail vehicles and commercial trucks and buses.
markets: Supplies train builders, truck makers and operators across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Industrial B2B brand with no consumer marketing; F1 offers only limited hospitality value.

name: BorgWarner
desc: Automotive supplier of turbochargers, drivetrain components, electric drive modules, battery systems and charging for vehicle makers.
markets: Production in about 24 countries serving carmakers and commercial vehicle makers worldwide.
rationale: Powertrain supplier with Indianapolis 500 trophy heritage; F1 offers engineering showcase and OEM hospitality.
changed: Spun off fuel systems and aftermarket business, including the Delphi brand, as PHINIA in 2023

name: Michelin
desc: French tyre maker selling Michelin, BFGoodrich and Kleber tyres to carmakers, fleets and consumers, and publishing the Michelin Guide.
markets: Sells worldwide across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific, South America and Africa.
rationale: Global consumer brand active in WEC, MotoGP and Le Mans; F1 offers premium reach, though Pirelli supplies F1 tyres.

name: Bridgestone Corporation
desc: Japanese tyre and rubber maker selling Bridgestone and Firestone tyres, auto services and diversified rubber products.
markets: Sells worldwide; Bridgestone Americas based in Nashville serves North and Latin America.
rationale: Global brand and long-time Olympic sponsor with past F1 tyre supply; F1 offers premium reach, though Pirelli supplies tyres.

name: KLA Corporation
desc: Makes process control, inspection and metrology equipment and software for semiconductor and electronics manufacturers.
markets: Customers are chipmakers in Taiwan, South Korea, China, US, Japan and Europe.
rationale: Pure B2B equipment supplier with a small customer base and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Gestamp
desc: Spanish supplier of stamped and press-hardened metal body, chassis and structural components for carmakers.
markets: Plants in more than 20 countries across Europe, Americas and Asia serving global carmakers.
rationale: B2B supplier with no consumer brand; F1 only plausible as hospitality for carmaker clients.

name: Zeekr
desc: Chinese premium electric vehicle brand making the Zeekr 001, 007, 009 and X models for consumers.
markets: China core market; sells in Europe, Middle East, Asia-Pacific and other export markets.
rationale: Premium EV brand building awareness abroad; F1 fits, decisions likely taken at Geely Auto level.
changed: Listed on NYSE in 2024; taken private and fully absorbed by Geely Automobile Holdings in 2025

name: Hyundai Mobis
desc: South Korean auto parts maker supplying chassis, cockpit and front-end modules, electrification parts, sensors and aftersales parts.
markets: Supplies Hyundai and Kia plants worldwide and other carmakers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B supplier tied to Hyundai Motor Group, which is absent from F1; limited but plausible hospitality value.

name: Horse Powertrain
desc: Develops and builds combustion engines, hybrid systems and transmissions for Renault, Geely brands and other carmakers.
markets: Plants and R&D in Europe, Brazil, China and Turkey serving carmakers in several regions.
rationale: Co-owners Renault (Alpine team owner) and Aramco (F1 partner) link it to F1 indirectly; B2B brand with limited marketing.
changed: Created as Renault-Geely joint venture in 2024; Aramco agreed to take a 10% stake

name: Rimac Group
desc: Croatian group developing electric hypercars and supplying battery systems and electric drivetrains to carmakers.
markets: Rimac Technology supplies European carmakers; Bugatti Rimac sells hypercars to wealthy buyers worldwide.
rationale: Performance EV technology brand with Bugatti hypercars; F1 fits engineering credibility and luxury hypercar positioning.

name: Garmin
desc: Makes GPS smartwatches, fitness wearables, cycling computers, marine electronics, aviation avionics and automotive navigation systems.
markets: Sells to consumers and OEMs worldwide across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Consumer wearables brand with sports sponsorship culture; F1 fits performance data and global reach.

name: Chery Holding Group
desc: Chinese state-controlled automotive group whose Chery Automobile makes Chery, Exeed, Jetour, Omoda and Jaecoo vehicles.
markets: China plus exports to over 80 countries across Russia, Middle East, Latin America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Major exporter growing in Europe and emerging markets; F1 offers international consumer awareness.
changed: Subsidiary Chery Automobile listed in Hong Kong in 2025

name: Linamar
desc: Canadian manufacturer of precision powertrain and driveline components, Skyjack access equipment and MacDon agricultural machinery.
markets: Operations in about 17 countries across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B manufacturer with little marketing culture; weak F1 fit beyond engineering hospitality.

name: Seres Group
desc: Chinese carmaker producing AITO electric and range-extender SUVs with Huawei, plus engines and other vehicles.
markets: Sales mainly in China; limited exports and no verified large-scale expansion plans.
rationale: Fast-growing Chinese EV maker with little presence abroad; F1 relevant only if it pushes exports.
changed: Renamed Seres Group from Sokon Group in 2022

name: ABB
desc: Swiss-Swedish technology group making electrification, automation and motion products for utilities, industry, transport and buildings.
markets: Operates in about 100 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Formula E title sponsor; rivals Siemens and Schneider sponsor F1, so strong B2B fit.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to sell its robotics division to SoftBank

name: BMW Group
desc: German maker of luxury BMW, MINI and Rolls-Royce cars and BMW Motorrad motorcycles.
markets: Sells about 2.5 million vehicles a year across more than 140 countries.
rationale: Premium global brand with F1 history; F1 suits premium positioning, though it competes in other series.

name: GAC Group
desc: Chinese state-controlled carmaker producing GAC Trumpchi, Aion and Hyptec vehicles and joint-venture Toyota and Honda cars.
markets: China main market; growing exports to Middle East, South-East Asia, Latin America and Europe.
rationale: Exporter seeking international awareness; F1 plausible, though state-owned decision-making slows sponsorship spending.

name: Sonic Automotive
desc: US automotive retailer running franchised new-car dealerships, EchoPark used-car stores and powersports dealerships.
markets: Customers in the United States only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: US-only car retailer; F1 relevant only through the three US races, so a weak fit.

name: Mitsubishi Motors
desc: Japanese carmaker producing SUVs, pickups and passenger cars, including the Outlander, Triton and Pajero Sport.
markets: Major sales in South-East Asia, Oceania, North America, Europe and Japan.
rationale: Consumer brand with rally heritage strong in Asia; F1 plausible but budgets constrained.

name: Dana
desc: Supplier of axles, driveshafts, transmissions, e-motors, sealing and thermal products for light and commercial vehicles.
markets: Operations in about 30 countries serving vehicle makers in North America, Europe, South America and Asia.
rationale: B2B drivetrain supplier with motorsport components history; F1 plausible only as customer hospitality.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to sell its Off-Highway business to Allison Transmission

name: Piaggio Group
desc: Italian maker of scooters and motorcycles under Vespa, Piaggio, Aprilia and Moto Guzzi, plus light commercial vehicles.
markets: Sells in Europe, India, Vietnam and other Asian markets, and the Americas.
rationale: Iconic Italian consumer brands with Aprilia in MotoGP; F1 plausible for premium two-wheel marketing.

name: Apollo Tyres
desc: Indian tyre maker selling Apollo and Vredestein tyres for cars, trucks, buses, farm vehicles and two-wheelers.
markets: About 87% of revenue from India and 11% from Europe; plants in India, Netherlands and Hungary.
rationale: Sports-sponsoring tyre brand with European ambitions; F1 plausible, though Pirelli is the exclusive F1 tyre supplier.

name: Tata Motors
desc: Indian maker of commercial vehicles including trucks, vans and buses, part of the Tata Group.
markets: India core market; exports to South Asia, Africa, Middle East and other emerging markets.
rationale: Strong brand in India with planned Iveco takeover adding Europe; F1 plausible for B2B hospitality.
changed: Passenger vehicles and JLR demerged into Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles in October 2025; agreed to acquire Iveco Group in 2025
f1: Agreed to acquire Iveco (F1 partner) in 2025; completion not confirmed here

name: TVS Motor Company
desc: Indian maker of motorcycles, scooters, electric scooters and three-wheelers, owning Norton Motorcycles.
markets: India core market; exports to over 80 countries across Asia, Africa, Latin America and Europe.
rationale: Motorsport-active consumer brand expanding abroad with Norton; F1 offers international brand reach.

name: Isuzu Motors
desc: Japanese maker of trucks, buses, D-Max pickups and diesel engines for commercial and consumer customers.
markets: Sold in about 100 countries, strong in Japan, South-East Asia, Australia and other markets.
rationale: Mainly commercial vehicle brand with limited global marketing; F1 plausible but not obvious.
changed: Acquired UD Trucks from Volvo Group in 2021

name: Voyah
desc: Premium electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle brand of Dongfeng Motor, selling SUVs, saloons and MPVs.
markets: China main market; exports to Norway and other European markets, Middle East and South-East Asia.
rationale: Premium EV brand building awareness abroad; F1 plausible, but state ownership slows sponsorship decisions.
changed: Dongfeng announced plans in 2025 to list Voyah in Hong Kong

name: Nokian Tyres
desc: Finnish tyre maker known for winter tyres, selling car, van, truck and heavy tyres and running Vianor retail.
markets: Nordics, Central Europe and North America; plants in Finland, the US and Romania.
rationale: Niche premium tyre brand in Nordics and North America; F1 offers limited fit, Pirelli is exclusive supplier.
changed: Exited Russia in 2022 and sold its Russian operations in 2023

name: CEAT
desc: Indian tyre maker producing tyres for two-wheelers, cars, trucks, buses, tractors and off-highway vehicles.
markets: India core market; exports to over 100 countries.
rationale: Cricket-sponsoring consumer brand with export growth; F1 plausible, though Pirelli is the exclusive supplier.

name: ABB E-mobility
desc: Makes DC fast chargers, AC wallboxes and charging software for fleets, charge-point operators and carmakers.
markets: Manufacturing in Europe, US and China; customers worldwide.
rationale: EV charging supplier linked to ABB's Formula E title role; F1 fit limited by combustion-hybrid focus.

name: Harley-Davidson
desc: US maker of cruiser and touring motorcycles, parts, accessories and apparel sold through dealers.
markets: Sells in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America through dealers.
rationale: Iconic lifestyle brand; F1 plausible via US races, though its audience leans toward other motorsports.

name: Volvo Group
desc: Swedish maker of trucks, buses, construction equipment and marine and industrial engines under Volvo, Mack and Renault Trucks.
industry: truck, bus and construction equipment maker
markets: Sells in about 190 markets across Europe, North and South America, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: Strong B2B brand selling to fleets and contractors; F1 plausible for hospitality, not an obvious fit.
changed: Sold Volvo Cars to Ford in 1999 and UD Trucks to Isuzu in 2021

name: Chery Automobile
desc: Chinese carmaker selling petrol, hybrid and electric cars under Chery, Exeed, Jetour, Omoda, Jaecoo and iCar brands.
markets: China plus exports to over 80 countries across Russia, Middle East, Latin America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Major exporter building brand awareness in Europe and emerging markets; F1 offers international consumer reach.
changed: Listed in Hong Kong in 2025

name: Mahindra & Mahindra
desc: Indian maker of SUVs, pickups, commercial vehicles, tractors and electric vehicles, flagship of the Mahindra Group.
markets: India core market; tractors and vehicles sold in the US, South Africa, Australia, Europe and other markets.
rationale: Formula E team owner with strong brand marketing; F1 plausible for international SUV and tractor ambitions.

name: Denso
desc: Japanese supplier of thermal, powertrain, electrification, electronics and safety systems to carmakers, Toyota its largest customer.
markets: Operations across Japan, North America, Europe and Asia; North American base in Southfield, Michigan.
rationale: Global Tier 1 supplier with motorsport history; F1 offers engineering showcase and hospitality.

name: Ninebot
desc: Chinese maker of Segway and Ninebot electric scooters, e-bikes, off-road vehicles and robotic lawnmowers.
markets: Sells worldwide through retail and online channels in Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Consumer e-mobility brand with global retail presence; F1 plausible for youth and urban audiences.
changed: Acquired Segway Inc. in 2015

name: Honeywell Aerospace
desc: Makes aircraft engines, auxiliary power units, avionics, navigation, environmental control and space systems for aircraft and defence customers.
markets: Commercial airline, business aviation and defence customers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Middle East.
rationale: B2B aerospace supplier; F1 plausible as engineering showcase and hospitality, not an obvious fit.
changed: Separated from Honeywell as a standalone company in 2026

name: Bombardier
desc: Canadian manufacturer of Challenger and Global business jets, with aircraft servicing and defence variants.
markets: Sells to corporate, private and government buyers across North America, Europe, Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Business-jet buyers overlap F1 Paddock Club audience; hospitality fits; jet operators Flexjet and VistaJet already sponsor F1.
changed: Sold rail business to Alstom in 2021

name: Qnity Electronics
desc: Supplies materials for semiconductor and electronics manufacturing, including polishing pads, slurries, photoresists and Kapton films.
markets: Customers are chipmakers and electronics manufacturers in Asia, North America and Europe.
rationale: B2B materials supplier to a narrow base of chipmakers with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.
changed: Spun off from DuPont in November 2025

name: Rolls-Royce Holdings
desc: British maker of civil and defence aircraft engines, nuclear submarine reactors and mtu power systems.
markets: Customers are airlines, aircraft makers and governments worldwide.
rationale: Global engineering brand; F1 plausible for technology showcase, though it markets mainly B2B.

name: Air China
desc: Chinese flag carrier operating domestic and international passenger and cargo flights from Beijing and Chengdu hubs.
markets: China plus international routes to Asia, Europe, North America and Oceania.
rationale: Major airline with Chinese Grand Prix tie potential; F1 plausible but state-controlled decisions.

name: Air France-KLM
desc: Franco-Dutch airline group operating Air France, KLM and Transavia passenger airlines, cargo and engineering services.
markets: Hubs in Paris and Amsterdam with routes across Europe, Americas, Africa, Asia and Middle East.
rationale: Major European airline group; airline rivals sponsor F1, so travel partnership fits.
changed: Formed by merger of Air France and KLM in 2004

name: AviLease
desc: Saudi aircraft leasing company buying narrow- and wide-body aircraft and leasing them to airlines.
markets: Leases aircraft to airlines in several regions; owned by Saudi Public Investment Fund.
rationale: B2B lessor with no consumer brand; F1 relevant only via Saudi Grand Prix hospitality.

name: Azul
desc: Brazilian airline operating mainly domestic passenger flights, with some international routes and the TudoAzul loyalty programme.
markets: Mostly Brazilian domestic network, plus routes to the US and Europe.
rationale: Brazilian consumer airline brand, but Chapter 11 restructuring makes significant F1 spending unlikely.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US in 2025

name: Dubai Aerospace Enterprise
desc: Aviation services company leasing commercial aircraft through DAE Capital and providing maintenance through DAE Engineering.
markets: Serves over 200 airline customers in more than 85 countries.
rationale: B2B lessor owned by Dubai government; F1 plausible only for Gulf hospitality.

name: IndiGo
desc: Indian low-cost airline operating Airbus and ATR aircraft on domestic and international routes.
markets: India dominant; international routes to Asia, Middle East and Europe.
rationale: Largest Indian airline with mass audience; F1 plausible as it expands long-haul, modest fit.

name: Samvardhana Motherson International
desc: Indian supplier of wiring harnesses, mirrors, bumpers, plastic modules and other components to carmakers.
markets: Plants in about 40 countries across Europe, Americas and Asia supplying global carmakers.
rationale: B2B supplier to German and Japanese carmakers; F1 plausible for hospitality, not obvious.

name: Lufthansa
desc: German airline group operating Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian, Brussels Airlines and Eurowings, plus Lufthansa Technik and cargo.
markets: Hubs in Frankfurt, Munich, Zurich and Vienna, flying to all world regions.
rationale: Major European airline group; rival airlines sponsor F1, so travel partnership fits.
changed: Acquired a stake in ITA Airways in 2025

name: Embraer
desc: Brazilian aircraft maker producing regional jets, business jets, military transport aircraft and defence systems.
markets: Sells to airlines, governments and private owners worldwide; operations in US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Business-jet clients overlap F1 hospitality audience; plausible through Brazilian and US races.

name: Coherent
desc: Makes optical networking transceivers, lasers, silicon carbide and engineered materials for data-centre, industrial and semiconductor customers.
markets: Customers are data-centre, telecom, industrial and semiconductor companies across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B photonics supplier riding AI data-centre demand; F1 plausible only as technology hospitality.
changed: Renamed from II-VI to Coherent in 2022 after acquiring Coherent Inc.

name: Polaris
desc: US maker of off-road vehicles, snowmobiles, Slingshot three-wheelers, boats and military vehicles sold through dealers.
markets: Mainly North America; also sells in Europe, Asia-Pacific and other markets.
rationale: Powersports brand with racing culture; F1 plausible via US races, not core audience.

name: Air Canada
desc: Canada's flag carrier, flying passengers and cargo to about 200 destinations, with Aeroplan loyalty programme.
markets: Canada core market; routes across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Strong Canadian consumer brand; Canadian Grand Prix gives a natural F1 tie-in.

name: GE Aerospace
desc: US maker of commercial and military jet and turboprop engines, with CFM joint venture and engine services.
markets: Airline, aircraft maker and defence customers worldwide across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Middle East.
rationale: Engineering brand with high technology tie-in potential; F1 offers B2B hospitality with airline customers.
changed: Renamed GE Aerospace in 2024 after spinning off GE HealthCare and GE Vernova

name: Dassault Systèmes
desc: French software company selling 3D design, simulation and product lifecycle software such as CATIA and SOLIDWORKS.
markets: Industrial customers across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Rival Siemens and Synopsys-Ansys sponsor F1; engineering software showcase makes F1 a natural fit.

name: Airbus
desc: European maker of commercial aircraft, helicopters, military aircraft and satellites for airlines and governments.
markets: Customers worldwide; main operations in France, Germany, Spain, UK, US and China.
rationale: Rival Boeing is an F1 partner; Airbus could use F1 for engineering showcase and B2B hospitality.

name: Larsen & Toubro
desc: Indian conglomerate in engineering, construction, infrastructure, energy projects, defence equipment and IT services.
markets: India core market; projects in the Middle East, Africa and Asia; IT services worldwide via LTIMindtree.
rationale: Domestic giant with Middle East presence; F1 plausible for Gulf B2B hospitality.

name: Aena
desc: Spanish airport operator managing 46 Spanish airports and holdings in London Luton and Brazilian airports.
markets: Spain core; airports in UK (Luton) and Brazil, plus stakes in Mexico and Colombia.
rationale: Infrastructure operator with little sponsorship need; weak F1 fit beyond Madrid race tie-in.

name: Air India
desc: Indian flag carrier flying domestic and international passenger routes with Airbus and Boeing aircraft.
markets: India plus routes to North America, Europe, Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Tata-owned airline rebuilding globally; sister firm Tata Communications and part-owner Singapore Airlines are F1 partners.
changed: Returned to Tata Group in 2022; merged with Vistara in 2024

name: Divergent Technologies
desc: Uses AI-driven design and metal 3D printing to make lightweight structures for carmakers, aerospace and defence.
markets: US-based; customers include European and American carmakers and US defence contractors.
rationale: Advanced-manufacturing brand with hypercar links through Czinger; F1 fits as a lightweight-engineering technology showcase.

name: Textron
desc: US industrial conglomerate making Cessna and Beechcraft aircraft, Bell helicopters, defence systems and specialised vehicles.
markets: Customers in the US and worldwide, including militaries and business aviation operators.
rationale: Business aviation brands suit hospitality, but defence focus weakens fit; plausible but not obvious.

name: Deutsche Lufthansa
desc: German airline group operating Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian, Brussels Airlines and Eurowings, plus Lufthansa Technik and cargo.
